paragraphs: Waste Awareness Skills Training & Education — Uzbekistan

The project aims to develop and strengthen smart waste management competencies among university students in Uzbekistan through a comprehensive program of online and offline courses, workshops, and practical activities. By integrating digital tools, data analytics, and innovative technologies, students will learn how to design, implement, and optimize sustainable waste management solutions in both urban and rural settings. The project will encourage student-led innovation and entrepreneurship by supporting the creation of start-ups focused on circular economy practices, smart recycling systems, and eco-friendly technology solutions.

Through collaboration with two European Union universities, the project will bring international expertise and best practices to Uzbekistan, enhancing the quality of higher education in environmental technology and IT applications. It will foster intercultural exchange, joint curriculum development, and capacity building for faculty and students alike. By the end of the project, students will not only acquire theoretical knowledge but also practical skills, digital competencies, and entrepreneurial experience, empowering them to contribute actively to sustainable development and smart environmental management in Uzbekistan.

This initiative aligns with national priorities for environmental sustainability, innovation, and higher education modernization, positioning participating universities as leaders in promoting technological solutions for waste management.
Keywords: environmental sustainability; Green Deal; smart waste management skills; student-led innovation; green transformation; eco-friendly technology solutions; green skills.

paragraphs: Waste Awareness Skills Training & Education — Uzbekistan
The project is organised in six interlinked work packages, each led by one partner. Together they total 122 person-months over 36 months.
WP1 — Project Management, Financial and Quality Monitoring Framework

Coordinate the efforts of all partners and support them throughout the project; collect cost statements from partners, submit financial reports to the EU and transfer released funds to partners; submit reports and financial statements; deliver the interim and final internal quality (QAB) reports and the external evaluator reports. Baseline data on students’ competencies and institutional capacities in smart waste management are collected early.
WP2 — Development of Innovative Teaching Framework and Methodology

Students gather information on waste management practices in different cities of Uzbekistan; researchers analyse the information and recommend the most appropriate focus areas for subsequent work; methodological guidelines, manuals and a comprehensive handbook are prepared.
WP3 — Curriculum Development and Training Implementation

Fergana State Technical University leads development of an online short course that embeds sustainability and smart waste management into formal higher education curricula; 20 workshops are run annually at schools, vocational schools and universities; the short course becomes a standard course within an existing curriculum; learning outcomes are assessed against objective criteria, contributing to the final grade and ECTS credits.
WP4 — Green Innovation Hub and Virtual Laboratory
Set up laboratory experiments on down-selected waste management practices; build a Virtual Laboratory that enables digital simulations and remote access to learning activities.
WP5 — Engagement with Industry and Entrepreneurship Support
Search for and select all key stakeholders and involve them actively in project activities; generate policies from project activities and present them to stakeholders.

Produce a communication, dissemination and sustainability plan for wide visibility and uptake of results at institutional, national and international levels; have every partner identify and involve its stakeholders; publish research papers at international conferences and in peer-reviewed journals.

paragraphs: The WASTE-UZ consortium unites six higher education institutions with complementary expertise: four from Uzbekistan and two European universities (Spain and Türkiye). Each lead one work package. The project is funded by the European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA) under Erasmus+.
